html:
An epidemic that struck the Hittite kingdom for some twenty years in the late 1300s BCE. It is known from the prayers of King Mursili II, which are among the most personal texts to survive from the ancient Near East.

The disease is said to have come with Egyptian prisoners taken in a war in Syria under Mursili's father, Suppiluliuma I. It killed Suppiluliuma and then his son and heir, Arnuwanda II, which put the young Mursili on the throne.

In his plague prayers Mursili asks the gods why the dying goes on. He searches old tablets for a sin and finds two: offerings to a river god that had been neglected, and a broken treaty with Egypt. He confesses his father's guilt and pleads that the gods stop punishing a land with no one left to bring them offerings. The war with Egypt that spread the plague went on, and led a generation later to the Battle of Kadesh.
